An **anxiety hangover** —commonly called **hangxiety** —is ` [Highlight start] a wave of worry, dread, or uneasiness that shows up after drinking alcohol [Highlight end] ` . It happens as alcohol wears off and your brain tries to rebalance its chemistry, compounded by poor sleep, dehydration, and blood sugar dips. (A similar lingering exhaustion and unease can also happen after a panic attack.)[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXtCeGjobyepJcGSVzlXINPzz9-T-rKUXN3IHw7bedLWqdDJM-R85L3275LQvAFTMBgZaoJlqTzOuJhO4theUDRnjnH2Gr7RqWmHMtjSbUAzZogW5D_cckhtK9nlzfIUo36erwLw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF16rYjAH66kYI47KsP2zpN5O216B1hfXr0OUxjEYx9qGl3b047Vlr92swsJtP9fkPVQpPMb44oHkkyJugAVdNyBcI3OF7VZgdYIifq4AtGbZiD5-BnrSW9EYpHWiI8USgz1EyT1DAAdYhkEYWvLb7U3Um1oexiFxV-GX8qF3m45SF2AIN)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1_wJeHUnIgEHO2WsgX3DrQAqSLDCADhUSxz3o6frlH69BcH7434pvpJTxNR7uyJmL2wQ1lEWZUVP28QdygJvTXLisFnYg3E3CjDEmXfR0GIWBj_AaBiBRVIJB3zgFzyMMoDTQQw4pmOiDNqni5ujG_uK22nMm9Q6WDfMGO-zLYKA6_AAFgyu2qWX7bSjLFW_yg)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAES4gEBxCJF1_rdNFn-0To46C_a-D3J-A4jvqw_aVP7JWLe8nw_TXyrkSFjojnaDRu9lL3f7fyDMlhaloBbY6mk4gc59svqVI9jkuqi4TypsjKHgvrYp-7eJKkowonMyXrk_y044bxVWFQZP6dmdSeK9ljjP4cMFS7mTdCp1nFh9Dx64T305odHlkF8Y42Wbafe4ugZGGbp8e9Wl11pV1GIkmPFfo2nnBbSzQIgjwOE6y18dQRl2of9qjh0bMdH5jMqoKebuhyk1RfEI_aNcnasxaT5dPptCWNwOELoKPRb0bscjGYH)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF1_3x2LFZC_yHtfW-0ZPh3wug_c5-OaKsL1hQmMPNVYr0YpLizOdYYnhB_uJgU2daNI05t9yTDflH5nzBB6sTj2HTzxkAdMpsHcOB8BybEivP5u2w1VcdJUPYdKZkUZMQ3EuXghl81fYlGLVB1EhjqfiYYwpZf_z58rkeIrn2dCQZB6SHggK3)

### Common Symptoms

- **Emotional:** Unease, a sense of impending doom, racing thoughts, irritability, or embarrassment and regret over things said or done.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1_wJeHUnIgEHO2WsgX3DrQAqSLDCADhUSxz3o6frlH69BcH7434pvpJTxNR7uyJmL2wQ1lEWZUVP28QdygJvTXLisFnYg3E3CjDEmXfR0GIWBj_AaBiBRVIJB3zgFzyMMoDTQQw4pmOiDNqni5ujG_uK22nMm9Q6WDfMGO-zLYKA6_AAFgyu2qWX7bSjLFW_yg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjQEBxCJF11myIzX5y540p9hUEhNBP0pnhfIJm4a0gnBM5VboI7SPiStKKv-ROWFwJhwc-Kk71Nb2wzbOcIjc75a_G3HS5UVwr6thTGrxYMntRMQOubgcZ1v7l02ozONuGVu5bYA-FOB--NJDK510eVQi1SQIcINtDoSZcd2uDImfUz4elq1ojwyrB2VvKTs)
- **Physical:** Racing or pounding heartbeat, sweating, shakiness, dizziness, nausea, headache, or fatigue.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXXB3RljttivRRyHC4p_1B2pjzkK15SHVaJUk3NHhbBHq4Ggr713WaNYfiPiBcSNex4m1lH4XEk2469RDyvfgizuAukuHE2DtXs3HrGtuIQJNm7fFZAklQPhH27iV9V2JZ4-bfKUyp0HfXJIcskuk9oU1LfUltrUxQYocI)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXUdTht183J3fi9NXtb1CcdjLsYaHIYwk29TG2irA6xvT7Kz_nBKJLENTykR2FedBFcYlrtfx2-QCvmKhpxx_27vlT7BKKsA7ULS4500snjD2BA5OFE8cWoKlrF8YYRFGpQOJzW_c)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESygEBxCJF17FwxUv4Y__DT3sRia0lgZUIsx82SOusOhfA18GXViZyv_kPhJ4uaVNupyGhtJw0eFCWa_FLy6TaFKd8Vv20ejBB3DpWPYgYJ1UAcJc2quOEbYp5IJ27vLrVI2yb2-QMscBgzc7R46EcsPzVqx5OXtjPlDfYyWxnMJCgM0XnBFH_dJ9PU-W5oEFzcHDDjbGz0qbwZuLITU6NcKoBrB59cUZENM0k1az33fDnKn_y3aYCHpQfLfv2vtW1100Ayi99jWv2Pplm)

### How Long It Lasts

Hangxiety usually peaks the next day and begins to fade within **24 hours** . Drinking more alcohol ("hair of the dog") may briefly dull the feeling, but it delays recovery and can stretch symptoms over multiple days.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF16rYjAH66kYI47KsP2zpN5O216B1hfXr0OUxjEYx9qGl3b047Vlr92swsJtP9fkPVQpPMb44oHkkyJugAVdNyBcI3OF7VZgdYIifq4AtGbZiD5-BnrSW9EYpHWiI8USgz1EyT1DAAdYhkEYWvLb7U3Um1oexiFxV-GX8qF3m45SF2AIN)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF17QVBrw8iwf3hrQ_UBwte9Gp9rVa0gDlwT-M7AMeQv_czP0HG_d1Kc0DCAVcgmVnW6WC4bZXxCpKtJEDRmgFuTeWEPc9kTo0UfLIgzub_AVnxNGvA4dhYoZjrmlwvaqRGHszDnVX3jjuodgVPNw8Jec8qoSZ_62nRDsVP6mD8SpT)

### Ways to Cope Right Now

- **Hydrate and eat:** Drink water or electrolytes and eat simple food to steady your blood sugar.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1_wJeHUnIgEHO2WsgX3DrQAqSLDCADhUSxz3o6frlH69BcH7434pvpJTxNR7uyJmL2wQ1lEWZUVP28QdygJvTXLisFnYg3E3CjDEmXfR0GIWBj_AaBiBRVIJB3zgFzyMMoDTQQw4pmOiDNqni5ujG_uK22nMm9Q6WDfMGO-zLYKA6_AAFgyu2qWX7bSjLFW_yg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXtCeGjobyepJcGSVzlXINPzz9-T-rKUXN3IHw7bedLWqdDJM-R85L3275LQvAFTMBgZaoJlqTzOuJhO4theUDRnjnH2Gr7RqWmHMtjSbUAzZogW5D_cckhtK9nlzfIUo36erwLw)
- **Skip stimulants and more alcohol:** Avoid caffeine and extra drinks, which can heighten jitteriness or prolong the rebound.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXtCeGjobyepJcGSVzlXINPzz9-T-rKUXN3IHw7bedLWqdDJM-R85L3275LQvAFTMBgZaoJlqTzOuJhO4theUDRnjnH2Gr7RqWmHMtjSbUAzZogW5D_cckhtK9nlzfIUo36erwLw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg)
- **Rest and ground yourself:** Rest, use slow breathing or distraction, and remind yourself that chemical rebound feelings are temporary. For a deeper breakdown of how brain chemistry shifts during recovery, [American Addiction Centers](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF16rYjAH66kYI47KsP2zpN5O216B1hfXr0OUxjEYx9qGl3b047Vlr92swsJtP9fkPVQpPMb44oHkkyJugAVdNyBcI3OF7VZgdYIifq4AtGbZiD5-BnrSW9EYpHWiI8USgz1EyT1DAAdYhkEYWvLb7U3Um1oexiFxV-GX8qF3m45SF2AIN) covers the physiological and psychological drivers in detail. For medical guidance on symptoms and recovery, see [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg) and the [Alcohol and Drug Foundation](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXtCeGjobyepJcGSVzlXINPzz9-T-rKUXN3IHw7bedLWqdDJM-R85L3275LQvAFTMBgZaoJlqTzOuJhO4theUDRnjnH2Gr7RqWmHMtjSbUAzZogW5D_cckhtK9nlzfIUo36erwLw).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXXtCeGjobyepJcGSVzlXINPzz9-T-rKUXN3IHw7bedLWqdDJM-R85L3275LQvAFTMBgZaoJlqTzOuJhO4theUDRnjnH2Gr7RqWmHMtjSbUAzZogW5D_cckhtK9nlzfIUo36erwLw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXCLgmzKykNG8qqbl98YPjaNXFFAVTZ_dZI2_jVi66G34haZ1hTg0O80QL1WbS2kzqyYM7mhZtqgZl059cexjnxKQO7aY5_l_-qOoyC7yBl2rh_ufA2GLNpytbyNeTvS-whMMAH0vu)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF16rYjAH66kYI47KsP2zpN5O216B1hfXr0OUxjEYx9qGl3b047Vlr92swsJtP9fkPVQpPMb44oHkkyJugAVdNyBcI3OF7VZgdYIifq4AtGbZiD5-BnrSW9EYpHWiI8USgz1EyT1DAAdYhkEYWvLb7U3Um1oexiFxV-GX8qF3m45SF2AIN)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg)

### When to Seek Professional Help
Consider talking with a doctor or mental health professional if:

- Anxiety lasts for several days or keeps getting worse.
- You rely on alcohol to cope with stress, social anxiety, or low mood.
- You drink despite negative effects, or notice signs of alcohol dependence or withdrawal—get medical support before stopping heavy drinking abruptly.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXUdTht183J3fi9NXtb1CcdjLsYaHIYwk29TG2irA6xvT7Kz_nBKJLENTykR2FedBFcYlrtfx2-QCvmKhpxx_27vlT7BKKsA7ULS4500snjD2BA5OFE8cWoKlrF8YYRFGpQOJzW_c)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX2Wzx8DDbTXVWkWNJZwZ7DdhK_MRJiDFWdJoEeIolmuY-hjLnaaC9mjtfnEt8chYd59V2tP_pMVpctZfTLUIPzCA3hEyGTmzSP44AZdNLgByG8oE2A1keT1tzCIf9orFu_-gN04r42gONK0fhalmJR_OxNZrbDg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF16rYjAH66kYI47KsP2zpN5O216B1hfXr0OUxjEYx9qGl3b047Vlr92swsJtP9fkPVQpPMb44oHkkyJugAVdNyBcI3OF7VZgdYIifq4AtGbZiD5-BnrSW9EYpHWiI8USgz1EyT1DAAdYhkEYWvLb7U3Um1oexiFxV-GX8qF3m45SF2AIN)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1_wJeHUnIgEHO2WsgX3DrQAqSLDCADhUSxz3o6frlH69BcH7434pvpJTxNR7uyJmL2wQ1lEWZUVP28QdygJvTXLisFnYg3E3CjDEmXfR0GIWBj_AaBiBRVIJB3zgFzyMMoDTQQw4pmOiDNqni5ujG_uK22nMm9Q6WDfMGO-zLYKA6_AAFgyu2qWX7bSjLFW_yg)

items.title: Ways to Cope Right Now
items.text: Hydrate and eat: Drink water or electrolytes and eat simple food to steady your blood sugar. Skip stimulants and more alcohol: Avoid caffeine and extra drinks, which can heighten jitteriness or prolong the rebound. Rest and ground yourself: Rest, use slow breathing or distraction, and remind yourself that chemical rebound feelings are temporary. For a deeper breakdown of how brain chemistry shifts during recovery, American Addiction Centers covers the physiological and psychological drivers in detail. For medical guidance on symptoms and recovery, see Cleveland Clinic and the Alcohol and Drug Foundation.

items.text: Consider talking with a doctor or mental health professional if:
items.markdown: Consider talking with a doctor or mental health professional if:

items.text: Anxiety lasts for several days or keeps getting worse. You rely on alcohol to cope with stress, social anxiety, or low mood. You drink despite negative effects, or notice signs of alcohol dependence or withdrawal—get medical support before stopping heavy drinking abruptly.
